{{Quote|I formed the storm commandos and led them in their early missions. It was those successes that put us in a position to unleash a biological weapon, the Candorian plague, on Dentaal. We were just following orders. That was the last order I took from the Empire. I defected to the Alliance, but I'll be paying my debt to Dentaal until the day I die.|Crix Madine, ''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''|<ref name="Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
'''Crix Madine''' was an [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] [[Imperial officer|officer]] who formed and led the notorious [[Storm commando/Legends|Storm commandos]] of the Imperial military. In light of later missions, such as releasing a plague on [[Dentaal/Legends|Dentaal]], Madine defected to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], though it cost him his fiancée, [[Karreio]]. After several complications in his defection, Madine became a valuable part of the Rebellion, advising and leading [[Commando/Legends|commando]] operations. He also planned the successful commando raid on the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star's]] shield generator. After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Madine continued to serve in the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. He was killed in action by [[Durga Besadii Tai]] after being captured on a mission to sabotage the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|''Darksaber'']] superweapon.

==Biography==
{{Quote|I've come to the conclusion that those people who truly do great deeds don't feel the need to talk about them all the time.|Crix Madine|<ref name="Darksaber" />}}
===Imperial service===
[[File:Cmdr_Crix_Madine.png|thumb|left|200px|Commander Crix Madine of the Imperial Army]]
Born on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] no later than [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]],<ref name="DFRSB" /> Crix Madine attended the [[Raithal Academy/Legends|Raithal Academy]] and entered service in the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. He rose quickly through the ranks after establishing himself as an innovative tactician and effective leader. He was engaged to a woman named [[Karreio]]. When the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] identified a need for a surgical strike force to counter the Alliance's guerrilla tactics, Madine was selected to form the unit. The result was the [[Storm commando/Legends|Storm commandos]], which Madine hand picked from the stormtrooper ranks and trained himself. He led the unit on a number of missions, but found the missions he and his men were called on to perform were increasingly questionable.<ref name="Darksaber" />

===Defection complications===
{{Quote|This contemptible excuse for an officer will no longer divulge any more information to that Rebel, Kyle Katarn.|General [[Rom Mohc]] holding Madine at gunpoint on-board the ''[[Arc Hammer]]''|audio=ContemptibleExcuseForAnOfficer-DF.flac|<ref name="Star Wars: Dark Forces">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref>}}
He attempted to defect to the Alliance prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], and, to prove his loyalty, Madine provided essential guidance for the sabotage of [[Operation Strike Fear]] and the destruction of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Invincible (Strike Fear)|''Invincible'']].<ref>[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> 

After Yavin, he warned the Alliance about the [[Dark Trooper Project]]. During this period, Madine provided clues to the Rebellion; asked about [[Fest/Legends|Fest]], he confirmed the existence of a [[Weapons Research Facility]] there.<ref name="Star Wars: Dark Forces" />

However, it was the order to [[Dentaal Uprising|release]] the [[Candorian plague/Legends|Candorian plague]] on [[Dentaal/Legends|Dentaal]] that convinced Madine it was time to leave for good. Wracked with guilt over his role in the death of the entire Dentaalian population, Madine left his unit while performing a training mission about [[1 ABY/Legends|eleven months]] after the Battle of Yavin. Madine erased himself from Imperial records, although his disappearance was covered by some [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] news channels. He did not even tell his fiancée where he was going, not wanting to place her in a dangerous situation.<ref name="Darksaber" />

[[File:CrixMadineCaptured-DF.png|thumb|right|230px|Madine held at gunpoint by General Mohc aboard the ''Arc Hammer'', with Lord Vader observing]]
General [[Rom Mohc]], head of the Dark Trooper Project, discovered his defection and intercepted Madine's shuttle.<ref>''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> He was taken before Darth Vader on gunpoint, before imprisoned in [[Orinackra]], where he awaited execution. Upon learning of his capture, [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] dispatched [[Kyle Katarn]] to [[Mission to Orinackra|rescue]] Madine.<ref name="Star Wars: Dark Forces" />

[[File:CrixMadinePrison-DF.png|thumb|left|Madine in the [[Imperial Detention Center]], found by Kyle Katarn.]]
Upon his rescue, Madine revealed Mohc's role in the project, who solicited the help of [[smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]. He also provided the Alliance with intelligence on the Phases of the project and its stations, along with the existence of the ''Arc Hammer'' and a [[Ice Station Beta/Legends|Robotics Facility]], although their locations were unknown.<ref name="Star Wars: Dark Forces" />

After slipping back to his homeworld of Corellia, Madine's defection was intercepted once more by Imperial forces, but the [[Battle of Corellia (1 ABY)|timely arrival]] of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] allowed him to escape.<ref name="RS I">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>

===Rebel leader===
{{Quote|We have stolen a small Imperial shuttle. Disguised as a cargo ship, and using a secret Imperial code, a strike team will land on the moon and deactivate the shield generator.|Crix Madine|audio=Madine-Imperialshuttlestolen.flac|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
[[File:Madine_btm.jpg|thumb|left|200px|General Madine during the Battle of Endor.]]
Madine led a [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]] squadron named [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]] [[Liberation of Gerrard V|against]] Imperial forces on [[Gerrard V]]. He also led the ground forces on strikes with Rogue Squadron, including [[Battle of the Jade Moon|raid]] on the [[Jade Moon]] and [[Rescue on Kessel|Battle]] of [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]].<ref name="RS I" />

Madine usually accompanied his subordinate in field missions (such as missions alongside [[Risiev Credal]]), which earned him the respect of many Rebel soldiers. The [[Task Force on Alliance Security]], working alongside Madine in different missions, asked him to send a team of agents to recover designs by Imperial-aligned engineer [[Diran Miciluz]]. Madine also worked with the Task Force writing reports on threats to the Rebel Alliance, including the [[Granse Confederacy]] and [[Zayl Braith]]&mdash;Madine discovered that Braith was a fugitive of the Galactic Empire, and reported it to the Alliance.<ref name="air">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Madine led the ground forces in the [[Battle of Kothlis]] to recover the [[Razor (CR90 corvette)|''Razor'']] from the wreckage of the [[Motivator (Imperial-class)|''Motivator'']]. He also advised Rogue Squadron on many pivotal missions, including the [[Mission to Destrillion]], and the [[Battle of Dubrillion (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Dubrillion]], and the [[Fondor shipyard assault]].<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

[[File:Crix_Madine-LotDS.jpg|thumb|right|220px|General Crix Madine]]
His unit of Alliance commandos sabotaged a number of critical Imperial shipments to slow construction on the second Death Star and was responsible for the capture of the [[Tydirium/Legends|''Tydirium'']]. The most important battle of the war, the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], might never have happened without Madine, in fact, as [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] was extremely hesitant about killing Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], for she saw it as assassination, a tactic practiced only by criminals. Madine convinced her of the necessity of killing the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], and when it came time to plan the Alliance's strike on the Death Star, Madine was chosen to coordinate the destruction of the [[Endor/Legends|Sanctuary Moon]]-based shield generator.

===New Republic service===
{{Quote|Any last words?''"<br />"''Not to you.|Durga Besadii Tai and Crix Madine, shortly before the latter's execution|<ref name="Darksaber" />}}
Following the foundation of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], he turned down a seat on its [[Inner Council (New Republic)|Inner Council]], preferring to remain with the Republic's growing military. Instead he opted for the position of [[Field Commander/Legends|Field Commander]] of New Republic forces.<ref name="DFRSB" /> He eventually ascended to the [[New Republic Defense Force/Legends|New Republic Defense Force's]] highest intelligence post, [[Chief of Intelligence/Legends|Chief of Intelligence]], although he continued to operate in the field. Following the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|Seizure of Coruscant]], he learned that Karreio had died in the battle.<ref name="Darksaber" /> In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], he helped command ground forces at the [[Battle of Calamari]].

As [[Minister of the Army]] for the [[New Republic High Command/Legends|New Republic High Command]]<ref name="jasb">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> and [[Special Operations]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], Madine had given the [[New Republic Special Forces/Legends|New Republic Special Forces]] briefings on strategy for the [[Battle of the Maw]].<ref name="CotF">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref>

[[File:Madine_death.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Crix Madine killed by Durga Besadii Tai.]]
In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], Madine led a team to infiltrate the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]] and gather intelligence on the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|''Darksaber'']] project, but his teammates were soon killed, and he was captured. Prior to this mission, he had planted a tracker on Durga's vessel that allowed the New Republic to learn the location of the superweapon. Onboard the ''Darksaber'', Madine taunted one of his captors, the phony [[Sulamar]]. Boasting that his superweapon kept him safe from Republic reprisals, [[Durga Besadii Tai]] personally shot Madine through the heart, killing him instantly. Madine faced his end bravely without flinching, and the New Republic later brought about the destruction of the weapon.<ref name="Darksaber" />

===Legacy===
Following the resolution of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Madine was honored by the New Republic's successor state, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], with the construction of the [[General Crix Madine Military Reserve]] in orbit over [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. By [[137 ABY]], the [[Crix-class diplomatic courier shuttle|''Crix''-class diplomatic courier shuttle]] was named in his honor.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:CrixMadine-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|140px|General Madine]]

Several scenes were shot for ''Return of the Jedi'' where Madine is commanding a Mon Cal cruiser, shouting orders and such.

His death in [[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']] made him the first Rebel film character with a speaking role to be killed in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]. The distinction of first overall belongs to [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]], who was killed in [[Dark Empire II 1|''Dark Empire II'' 1]] almost a year prior to ''Darksaber''{{'s}} publication.

The decision to kill off his character was highly controversial with some fans. The group was small but vocal and felt that the character, as a favorite of theirs, should not have been killed off.<ref name="dorkery">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/158705254861/authors-notes-imperial-justice-pt-2|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=Jason Fry's Dorkery - Author's Notes: Imperial Justice, Pt. 2}}</ref>

Madine is incorrectly shown with white hair in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', unlike his hair in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']].

The ''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]'' mistakenly used Madine's image for the entry of [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]].

===Portrayal===
Crix Madine was portrayed by [[Dermot Crowley]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']].

[[Terence McGovern]] provided Madine's voice for [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]. [[Tom Kane]] provided his voice for ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''.

===Defection===
There is conflicting information about when Crix Madine defected. [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']] mentions him helping the Rebellion by masterminding the destruction of the [[Invincible (Strike Fear)|''Invincible'']] with the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustans]], ''before'' the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. In a part of ''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]'' that takes place ''after'' the battle, Mon Mothma says that Madine intended to defect to the Rebellion.
